question: In June 2025, up to what loan amount did the Reserve Bank of India raise the Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio on gold loans from 75% to 85%?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹2.5 lakhs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In **June 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** raised the **Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio** on gold loans from **75%** to **85%** for loans up to ₹**2.5 lakhs**.
 
• The decision was taken to provide greater liquidity to borrowers, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas where gold loans are prevalent.
 
• The LTV ratio indicates the maximum percentage of the gold's market value that can be provided as a loan. An increase from 75% to 85% means borrowers can avail a higher loan amount against the same quantity of gold.
 
• This measure aimed to support individuals and businesses in need of short-term credit during economic challenges or financial stress.
 
• Gold loans are a popular credit option in India due to their quick processing, minimal documentation, and lower interest rates compared to unsecured loans.
